title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 126
paragraphs: This was the counsel of Hecataeus; but Aristagoras was most inclined to go to Myrcinus. He therefore entrusted the government of Miletus to Pythagoras, a man of repute among the citizens, and sailed off to Thrace, taking with him everyone who wished to go; and he took possession of the region for which he had set out. But setting out from there to make war, he perished at the hands of the Thracians—both Aristagoras himself and his army—while he was encamped around a certain city and the Thracians wished to come out of it under a truce.
